links.outcome: Readability of AI summaries versus original notes (Flesch Reading Ease, grade level)
links.effect: AI summaries had Flesch Reading Ease 29.25 vs 56.89 for original notes and Grade 15.24 vs Grade 8.98; cosine similarity 0.6 showed moderate alignment.
links.quote: The AI summaries were harder to read, with a Flesch Reading Ease score of 29.25 compared to 56.89 for the original notes, and required a higher reading level—Grade 15.24 for the summaries versus Grade 8.98 for the original notes.

unlisted_practices: Structuring LLM summaries of clinical notes using the I-PASS handoff framework
Cosine similarity to measure alignment of AI summaries with source notes

screen.reason: Evaluates the feasibility, readability, and content alignment of an LLM (Mistral) for summarizing pediatric CVICU progress notes using automated readability and similarity metrics, without testing a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
